title: Dedicated capacity intake: commitment template and scaling governor
creator: Samantha Liu
description:
Problem: Sales and Solutions are frequently requesting committed dedicated pools with imprecise throughput targets and vague scaling expectations. This leads to last-minute reclassification of GPU family, unpredictable cost uplift, and overloaded runtime teams during onboarding.

Goal: Create a lightweight commitment template and a deterministic "scaling governor" policy that product, sales, and runtime can use during intake to: 1) bound SLAs for latency & throughput, 2) map workload profiles to GPU-class recommendations, and 3) define a default autoscaling governor (burst envelope, warm pool sizing, cooldowns, fallback routing).

Scope (non-bug): This ticket covers the product-side artifact (intake template, scoring matrix, and recommended defaults) and acceptance criteria for an initial pilot with two enterprise customers. Implementation of autoscaler changes and runtime enforcement will be tracked as engineering follow-ups.

Deliverables:
- Commitment template (form fields + example answers) for RM/SEs to collect on intake.
- A short scoring rubric that produces a numeric "commitment score" from workload inputs (expected steady throughput, p95 latency target, burst pattern, latency sensitivity, data residency, revenue criticality).
- GPU-class mapping guidance with conservative sizing rules and headroom percentages.
- Default scaling governor: recommended min/max pool sizes, burst credits, warm pool policy, cooldown window, and graceful-fallback steps (region/model fallback).

Proposed commitment template fields (example):
- Workload name and owner
- Typical steady QPS (tokens/sec or requests/sec) 
- Typical P95 response time target (ms)
- Maximum expected burst factor (x steady) and duration (mins)
- Request length distribution (median tokens, 90th percentile tokens)
- Preferred model family / quantization tolerance
- Data residency / privacy flags (contains PII? regulated?)
- Business criticality: test/dev | low | medium | high | blocking-production
- Desired SLA window (hours of day / 24x7)
- Expected growth horizon (3/6/12 months)
- Must-have constraints (budget cap, preemption allowed?)

Scoring rubric (high level): commitment_score = sum of weighted buckets (throughput_weight, latency_weight, burst_weight, criticality_weight, residency_weight). Produce three bands: Bronze (opportunistic reserved), Silver (committed with conservative scaling), Gold (hard SLOs + dedicated warm pool + priority preemption protection). Use the score to drive recommended SLA band and billing commitment suggestions.

GPU-class mapping examples (guideline only):
- Band Bronze: non-latency sensitive, < 1000 steady reqs, burst < 3x -> 1-2x A100-80GB equivalent; conservative headroom 30%
- Band Silver: latency sensitive p95 < 250ms, steady 1k-5k -> 2-8x A100/H100 family; headroom 40%
- Band Gold: p95 < 100ms or large-scale >5k steady or sub-100ms interactive workloads -> H100 family or larger; headroom 50% + warm pool.

Scaling governor (default policy):
- Min pool = baseline mapped from steady throughput (rounded up to nearest GPU unit).
- Max pool = Min pool * headroom_multiplier (1.5 - 2.0 based on band).
- Burst envelope: allow temporary burst above max for short durations using burst credits (token bucket with refill rate tied to billing commit).
- Warm pool: maintain N idle GPUs (N = ceil(0.1 * Min pool) for Silver, 0.25*Min for Gold) to absorb cold-start latency for queued kv-cache warmup.
- Cooldown: scale-down cooldown = 10m for interactive, 30m for batch.
- Graceful fallback: when capacity constrained for >2m, route new requests to lower-cost model variant or regionally adjacent pool (as defined in the routing policy).

Risk/trade-offs and notes:
- Conservative headroom increases cost; we will pair the template with a cost-impact table to set expectations for customers.
- Warm pools reduce unit cold-start latency but increase baseline cost. Offer as paid add-on for Gold commitments.
- Mapping tables must be revisited once we have actual perf profiles for targeted model family + quantization levels (ENG to supply perf curves).

Pilot plan:
1) Share draft template with Solutions and two committed enterprise customers (one SaaS conversational app, one embeddings-heavy retrieval app).
2) Run intake with both customers; compute commitment score and recommended config.
3) Align with ENG on perf experiments for one representative model and tweak headroom numbers.
4) Iterate and finalize template and ship a short Confluence page + example contract language incorporated into reserved-capacity quote wizard.

Acceptance criteria (must pass for Done):
- Template completed and approved by PM, Sales Engineering, and Runtime lead.
- Scoring rubric documented and produces expected band for two pilot customers with sample inputs.
- GPU mapping guidance reviewed by ENG and Runtime (sign-off from lead: should include explicit headroom numbers).
- Pilot intake run completed and feedback documented.
- Confluence doc and a short training slide deck for Sales/SEs published.
